newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UEFA OPPOSED TO WIMBLEDON'S MOVE TO DUBLIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA OPPOSED TO WIMBLEDON'S MOVE TO DUBLIN.

text.p: UEFA said on Wednesday it was totally opposed to English premier league Wimbledon relocating to Dublin and would not sanction the move.

UEFA spokesman Salvatore Cuccu stressed that the position of European soccer's governing body in the long-running saga had not changed, even if the London club were about to be taken over by a consortium of Irish businessmen including Paul McGuinness, the manager of rock group U2.
"UEFA are specific about this," he said. "Wimbledon are an English club with a home in England and UEFA is not in favour of them moving to a foreign country.

"It is okay to be innovative and look for new opportunities but this move would cause a great many problems. It is regrettable that a club from the home of football should be involved in a venture of this sort.
"It goes against the spirit of football, of crossing national boundaries and we are not in favour of it."
The move is also opposed in principle by the Football Association of Ireland. The English F.A. say they have no policy on the move as it has not yet been formally proposed to them.
Wimbledon are a poorly-supported team with crowds as small as 9,000 for premier league matches.
They have shared Selhurst Park with Crystal Palace eight kilometres away for the past five years but have always been eager to move back to their home neighbourhood.

The Irish consortium, led by McGuinness and property developer Owen O'Callaghan, have reportedly agreed to a deal which would enable them to purchase a 74 per cent shareholding in Wimbledon at a cost of around 20 million pounds ($30 million).
